finding.claim: notifyAll() sends a server-side POST to an attacker-supplied callback URL that was stored unvalidated by subscribe(). Each scheduled run (every minute) requests the attacker's chosen host, including internal or loopback addresses.
finding.source: src/Jobs.java:12-14 subscribe(name, callbackUrl): the POST /subscribe body field callbackUrl (per the comment at line 12) is stored in the static subscriptions map with no validation.
finding.sink: src/Jobs.java:21 URI.create(cb) and src/Jobs.java:24 client.send(req, ...) issuing a POST via the static HttpClient.

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe taking body fields name and callbackUrl. The route handler is not in this repository.
subscribe(name, callbackUrl) takes callbackUrl as a raw String.
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it with no scheme, host, port, or IP check.
notifyAll iterates subscriptions.values(), so every stored attacker URL is used.
URI.create(cb) parses the attacker string and builds the request target with no allowlist or private-address check.
POST body is the payload argument from the caller. It is not attacker-controlled in this file, so the attacker controls the destination, not the body.
client.send issues the request. The response body is discarded, so the attack is blind.

finding.guards_checked: (1) No validation at subscribe (line 14) or notifyAll (lines 19-21): no scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, or DNS resolution check. (2) Scheme: java.net.http.HttpClient only accepts http and https, so file:, gopher:, and similar schemes are blocked. Partial guard. (3) Redirects: HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so a 3xx from the attacker host is not followed to an internal target. Mitigates redirect-based pivots. (4) Response: body is discarded at line 24, so the attacker cannot read responses. Limits impact to blind requests. (5) Authentication/authorization on the /subscribe route is not visible in this repo, so I could not verify who can call subscribe(). (6) No timeouts set on the client or request, so a slow internal target can hang the loop. Availability concern, not SSRF itself. (7) URI.create throws IllegalArgumentException on a malformed entry, which aborts the notifyAll loop for the remaining subscribers. Availability concern, not SSRF itself.

verdict.guard_found: none: subscribe() (src/Jobs.java:13-14) stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and notifyAll() (src/Jobs.java:19-24) passes it to URI.create and client.send with no scheme, host, or private-IP check. The only validation in the file is the allowlist in thumb() (src/Jobs.java:30), which is not on this path. The repo search found no route handler or auth for /subscribe.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (src/Jobs.java:12-24) and no closing guard exists on the subscribe-to-notifyAll path, but the only evidence that callbackUrl is attacker-controlled is the comment at src/Jobs.java:12 documenting POST /subscribe, and the route handler and its authentication are not in this repository, so whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege caller can reach subscribe() cannot be decided here.
